entities.name: Childebert I
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Childebert I (born 497 CE in Reims; died December 23, 558 CE in Paris) reigned as King of Paris from 511 CE until his death, a pivotal period in the consolidation and expansion of the early Merovingian Frankish kingdom. As one of the four sons of Clovis I, the founder of the Frankish monarchy, Childebert inherited a significant portion of his father's realm, including the strategically vital city of Paris, which he established as his capital. His reign was characterized by relentless military campaigns, both independently and in concert with his brothers, aimed at expanding Frankish dominion over neighboring Visigothic and Burgundian territories, thereby shaping the geopolitical landscape of early medieval Western Europe.

Following the death of Clovis I in 511 CE, the Frankish kingdom was partitioned among his four sons, with Childebert receiving the central portion encompassing Paris, Orléans, Chartres, and parts of the Atlantic coast. He engaged in numerous military ventures, notably participating in the Frankish conquest of the Burgundian Kingdom alongside his brothers Chlothar I and Theuderic I between 523 and 534 CE, which brought significant new territories under Frankish control. Childebert also launched expeditions into Visigothic Septimania and Hispania, most famously besieging Zaragoza in 542 CE, from which he brought back the tunic of Saint Vincent, establishing the Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés to house the relic and serve as his final resting place. His campaigns, though not always decisive, consistently pressed Frankish claims and expanded their sphere of influence.
